plan.curriculum: Mathematics 2.0, Measurement, Year 6 (VC2M6M04): vertically opposite angles; use angle relationships to find unknown angles, communicating reasoning
plan.shape: example-first for the new fact, then mixed practice with all three facts, because the decision is which fact fits
plan.criticalFeature: vertically opposite angles are equal; say the angle fact with every answer
decisionPoints: the choice check: opposite or next to?
the hinge: two unknowns, two facts
plan.anchor: quarter turn 90°, half turn 180°, full turn 360°
plan.catchUp: Missed Session 3? Show one straight line with a known angle: the two parts make 180. That is the only earlier fact today needs.

manipulatives: Two rulers or pencils per student, to make crossing lines
A protractor for every student, to check answers
studentTools: Printed Worksheet for every student; Extension and Supported Worksheet as needed
routineIcons: Write it, chin it, show me
boardSetup: The anchor on the board: quarter turn 90°, half turn 180°, full turn 360°
Three angle facts listed: straight line 180°, point 360°, vertically opposite equal

resources.label: Worksheet
resources.description: Your turn. Opposite or next to, a which-fact table, a crossing sign and scissors, and a mistake to fix.
resources.title: Vertically Opposite Angles
resources.subtitle: Opposite angles are equal. Next to each other, they make 180°.

steps: m is on a straight line with 65°.

items.prompt: Which angle is opposite b?
Find a.
Find b.
Name the angle fact, then find the missing angle.
rows: Next to 64° where two lines cross
answers: Next to 64° where two lines cross

example.prompt: Two paths cross at 50°. What are the other three angles?
steps: Next to 50° on a straight line: 180° - 50° = 130°.

items.prompt: A railway crossing sign is an X. One angle is 124°. Find these angles.
Scissors are open so the blades make 28°. The handles cross at the same point. What angle do the handles make? How do you know?
items.answer: 28°. The handles are vertically opposite the blades, so the angle is equal.

example.prompt: Two lines cross. Could all four angles be 90°?
steps: Next to each other, they make 180°: 90° + 90° = 180°.
So yes: the lines are perpendicular.

items.prompt: Jordan found the angle opposite 65°. Find his mistake and fix it.
work: Two lines cross. One angle is 65°.
items.answer: Opposite angles are equal, so it is 65°. 115° is the angle next to it, on the straight line.

items.prompt: Two lines cross. Which list could be the four angles?
items.explain: Opposite angles match, and angles next to each other make 180°: 50 + 130 = 180.

resources.label: Extension
resources.description: Early finisher option. Three lines through a point, and angle proofs, with worked examples.
resources.title: Extension: Crossing Lines
resources.subtitle: Use all three angle facts together.

sections.title: Three lines through a point
sections.intro: When three straight lines cross at one point, there are six angles. Opposite angles are still equal, and all six make 360°.

example.prompt: Three lines make angles of 50° and 60° next to each other. Find the third angle in that half.
steps: The three angles on one side make a straight line: 180°.

items.prompt: Three lines cross. Two neighbouring angles are 40° and 75°. Find the third angle in that half-turn, then all six angles.
Three lines cross so all six angles are equal. How big is each?
items.explain: Six equal angles make a full turn: 360° shared by 6 is 60°.

items.prompt: Three lines cross. Two neighbouring angles are 90° and 35°. Find the other four angles.

example.prompt: Two lines cross. One angle is 2x and the one opposite is 80°. Find x.

items.prompt: One angle is 3y and the angle opposite is 105°. Find y.
Two neighbouring angles where lines cross are a and a + 40°. Find a.
Make your own number-sentence puzzle with crossing lines. Solve it.

steps: Colour 40° and the angle straight across from it.
They are opposite, so they are equal.

steps: d and 70° are next to each other on a straight line.

slides.notes: Session 4 of our angles week: today we find the angles where two lines cross.
Before you start, put two pencils or rulers, a board and a marker on every desk. Print the Worksheet for everyone, and a few copies of the Extension and the Supported Worksheet.

beats: SAY: Let's warm up with the four processes from last term.
ASK: What is 3 648 take away 1 979?
45 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 1 669
SCAN boards, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, next one.
Less -> model the first step on the board together, re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: The answer is 1 669. Tick it or fix it, and check by adding back.
trap: forgetting to regroup when the top digit is smaller.
Fix: regroup one column at a time, and they redo it.
notes.prep: Daily Review from Term 3 Week 7: four processes. Whole block under 7 minutes.

beats: SAY: The next one is a multiplication.
ASK: What is 48 times 25?
45 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 1 200
SCAN boards, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, next one.
Less -> model the first step on the board together, re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: The answer is 1 200. Tick it or fix it, and check by dividing back.
trap: multiplying only the ones.
Fix: split 48 into 40 and 8, and they redo it.

beats: SAY: And the last one is a division.
ASK: What is 1 452 divided by 6?
45 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 242
SCAN boards, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, then Fluency.
Less -> model the first step on the board together, re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: The answer is 242. Tick it or fix it, and check by multiplying back.
trap: dropping a place in the quotient.
Fix: multiply 6 by 242 to check, and they correct it.

slides.title: Add with the written method: 3 digits

beats: SAY: Now for some written addition.
Line up the places, and always start with the ones.
ASK: Use the written method to solve this one.
30 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 1 465
SCAN boards for the regrouped digits.
80%+ -> reveal, next one.
Less -> model the ones and the regroup together on the board, re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: The answer is 1 465. Tick it or fix it, and check every regroup.
trap: forgetting to add a regrouped ten.
Fix: circle each carried digit, and they add that column again.
notes.prep: Algorithm fluency: 3 digits, then 4, then 5. Whole block under 6 minutes.

SAY: The answer is 12 535. Tick it or fix it, and check every regroup.
trap: forgetting to add a regrouped ten.
Fix: circle each carried digit, and they add that column again.

slides.learningIntention: We are learning to use vertically opposite angles to find unknown angles and explain our thinking.
successCriteria: I can point to the pairs of vertically opposite angles where two lines cross.
I can find unknown angles where two lines cross.
I can explain each answer using an angle fact.

beats: POINT to the learning intention.
SAY: Today two straight lines cross, and we find all four angles they make.
SAY: Let's read our I can statements together. Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
SAY: Spotting the matching pairs is where we start,
and finding the unknown angles is our big goal today.
notes.prep: SC1 spotting pairs; SC2 finding unknowns is the core and the exit evidence; SC3 naming the fact is the stretch.

slides.title: Two lines cross
slides.prompt: Cross two pencils. How many angles? Which look the same size?

notes.answer: four angles; the opposite ones look the same
beats: SHOW two pencils crossing.
SAY: Take your two pencils and cross them, just like the lines on the screen.
ASK: How many angles can you see,
and which ones look the same size?
20 sec. Cue: Partner A first. You have 20 seconds. Go.
EXPECT: four; the ones opposite each other
SCAN pencils and listen for opposite.
80%+ -> name them vertically opposite, then move on.
Less -> trace each angle with a finger, compare the opposite pair, re-ask.
trap: seeing only two angles.
Fix: count around the point together until they find four.
notes.prep: Launch after the LI: students discover the pairs with their own crossed pencils. Under 4 minutes.

slides.meaning: Angles opposite each other where two straight lines cross. They are equal.
slides.example: If one is 50°, the angle opposite is 50° too.

notes.answer: angles opposite each other where two lines cross; they are equal
beats: POINT to the words. SAY: These words are vertically opposite. Say them with me.
SAY: Vertically opposite angles face each other across the point where the lines cross,
and they are always equal.
ASK: Can you point to the angle opposite the 50 degree angle?
5 sec. Cue: Voices off. Point... now. Hold your point.
EXPECT: pointing to the bottom angle
trap: thinking vertical means up and down.
Fix: explain it means at the vertex, and they point again.
notes.prep: Vertical here means at the vertex, not up and down: worth one sentence if asked.

slides.title: Opposite angles are equal
steps: b and 50° sit on a straight line.

beats: POINT to a and 50.
SAY: Angle a sits opposite the 50 degree angle, so they're equal.
That makes a 50 degrees.
POINT to b and 50 on the line.
SAY: Angle b and the 50 share a straight line, so together they make 180 degrees.
ASK: So how big is angle b?
10 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 130
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: It's 130 degrees. We used two facts:
opposite angles are equal, and a straight line is 180.
trap: saying b is 50 because it is nearby.
Fix: point to opposite, then next to, and they redo it.
notes.stretch: Find the fourth angle two different ways.
notes.help: Colour opposite pairs the same colour first.
notes.prep: Two facts working together: opposite equal, straight line 180. SC2.

beats: MODEL angle c first.
SAY: Angle c is on a straight line with the 115,
so 180 take away 115 is 65. That's the straight line fact.
ASK: How big is angle d, and which fact tells you?
10 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 115, vertically opposite
POINT to e.
SAY: Angle e sits opposite c, so e is 65 too. That's vertically opposite.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: Let's check all four: 115, 65, 115 and 65 make 360.
trap: giving answers with no fact.
Fix: ask which fact they used, and they add it.
notes.stretch: Why do the four angles always make 360?
notes.help: Sentence frame: ___ is opposite ___, so they are equal.
notes.prep: The reasoning habit: every answer carries its fact. SC3.

slides.title: Opposite or next to?
slides.prompt: Two lines cross. One angle is 70°. What is the angle opposite it?

options.misconception: uses the straight-line fact: thinks opposite means the angle next to it

beats: SAY: Look carefully: we want the angle opposite, not the one next to it.
ASK: If one angle is 70 degrees, what is the angle opposite it?
10 sec. Cue: Voices off. Point... now. Hold your point.
EXPECT: pointing to B
SCAN the room, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, then cold call one student: Where would 110 be?
Less -> cross two pencils, point opposite, then next to. Re-ask.
REVEAL after pointing is scanned.
SAY: It's B, 70 degrees, because vertically opposite angles are equal.
trap: pointing to A.
Fix: ask whether A is opposite or next to, and they choose again.
notes.prep: First decision point: A means the facts are mixed up, the most common error today.

slides.title: Find the angle, name the fact
slides.ask: Find the angle. Which fact did you use?
slides.pivot: cross two pencils and point: opposite or next to?
slides.followUp: cold call one board: say the fact out loud

items.say: 35 degrees. s and 145 share a straight line. Tick or fix.

say: and write the fact next to it.
trap: using the straight line for an opposite angle.
Fix: point to opposite or next to, and they redo it.
notes.stretch: Find all four angles in each diagram.
notes.prep: Guided practice mixing the two facts, so choosing the fact is the practice. SC2 and SC3.

notes.answer: t = 100°, u = 100°. 80 for u means the facts are mixed
beats: SAY: This one is just for you.
There are two answers, and two facts to name.
ASK: How big are angles t and u, and which fact tells you each one?
30 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: t = 100 straight line, u = 100 opposite
SCAN every board, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, then Your turn.
Less -> shade t, then point to u opposite it. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: Angle t is 100 degrees, from the straight line,
and u sits opposite t, so it's 100 too. Tick it or fix it.
trap: Fix: ask what u is opposite, and they redo it.
notes.prep: The hinge before independence. Students with u = 80 start with the teacher on the Supported Worksheet.

slides.title: Your turn
slides.task: Find the missing angles and name the facts on your worksheet.

beats: POINT to the steps.
SAY: Read each question carefully, solve it carefully, then check your answers.
SAY: If you finish, the Extension is your early finisher option.
Let's read the steps together. Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
CIRCULATE and ask: Which fact did you use?
TIME: 20 minutes. Stop everyone once at 10 minutes to share a strategy.
trap: answers with no fact.
Fix: ask which fact they used, and they add it.
notes.stretch: Extension: three lines through a point, and proofs.
notes.help: Supported Worksheet: sentence frames and a hint on every question.
notes.prep: Independent practice with all three facts, worded problems and reasoning. Sheet is evidence for SC2 and SC3.

slides.title: Show what you know
questions: Find v and write the fact.

beats: SAY: Here's the last one. Find v and write the fact on your board.
ASK: How big is angle v, and which fact tells you?
30 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 145, straight line
RECORD who writes 35 for v: opposite and next to are mixed.
They start next week's review with the teacher.
trap: writing 35.
Fix: none now. Record the name for next week.
notes.prep: Exit evidence for SC2 and SC3 across the week's facts.

slides.reflectionPrompt: Tell your partner the three angle facts from this week.

notes.answer: open - listen for straight line 180, point 360, opposite equal
beats: SAY: Let's read our I can statements together. Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
ASK: How sure are you that you can find angles where lines cross?
5 sec. Cue: Thumbs only, voices off. Show me... now.
EXPECT: thumbs up, sideways or down
RECORD each thumb down beside the exit board.
A thumb up with v = 35 matters most.
ASK: Tell your partner the three angle facts from this week.
20 sec. Cue: Partner B first. You have 20 seconds. Go.
EXPECT: straight line 180, point 360, opposite equal
notes.prep: Week close: the three facts, said aloud. Self-assessment read beside the exit evidence.
